patterns.platform: Carrd single-page sites (default sections / overlay text)
patterns.name: Low-opacity white text fails contrast while looking 'designed'
patterns.description: Carrd templates frequently set body/caption text in semi-transparent white (rgba(255,255,255,0.3) or 0.15) over photographic or gradient backgrounds. It reads as a tasteful muted style to the designer but falls far below 4.5:1, and over a varying photo background the effective ratio changes per region.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Subscribe for updates
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Automated contrast tools can't reliably compute the ratio of text over a CSS background-image/photo (no solid color to sample) and often skip or guess; the rgba opacity composited against an image is exactly the case scanners punt on, leaving a human to sample the rendered pixels.
patterns.realWorldNote: Audit of a Carrd site found 50 automated issues incl. text using rgba(255,255,255,0.3) and rgba(255,255,255,0.15) weakening contrast. https://dev.to/yuridevat/accessibility-check-2-195p

patterns.name: Light-gray body/caption text below 4.5:1 in the default palette
patterns.description: Many Wix templates ship with light-gray secondary text (captions, subtitles, footer text, form helper text) that fails AA contrast out of the box. Because it's the template default, it propagates everywhere the user adds that text style without them realizing it's non-compliant.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Crafted with care since 2014
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably caught by axe/Lighthouse when text sits on a solid color — included for completeness. The judgment-light cases (solid background, real text node) are auto-detectable; only the over-image variants need a human.
patterns.realWorldNote: Wix ADA guides repeatedly cite 'many Wix templates use light gray text that fails contrast requirements' as a default-template problem. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility

patterns.platform: Squarespace image-caption overlay (dark-overlay style) & gallery captions
patterns.name: Caption text over a dark-overlay/photo overlay fails contrast
patterns.description: The built-in 'dark overlay' caption style puts light caption text over a semi-transparent dark scrim on top of a photo. On bright or busy images the scrim isn't enough and the foreground/background ratio drops below 4.5:1 in some regions of the image while passing in others.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Text over a translucent scrim over a photo has no single computable background color; scanners cannot evaluate per-pixel contrast across the image and typically skip it, so a human must visually sample worst-case regions.
patterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Dark overlay option produces poor foreground/background color contrast' for image captions. https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

patterns.platform: Shopify Dawn / Debut — sale badges and disabled/sold-out states
patterns.name: Insufficient contrast on sale badges and disabled buttons
patterns.description: 'Sale' / 'Sold out' badges and disabled 'Add to cart' buttons use light or theme-accent colors (e.g. light pink on white, grey-on-grey) that fall below 4.5:1 for the text, and the badge's non-text boundary can fall below 3:1. Common in default and lightly-customized Dawn/Debut palettes.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This is largely auto-detectable: axe/Lighthouse compute text contrast ratios and flag <4.5:1. Edge cases tools may miss are disabled-control text (some scanners skip disabled elements) and badge text over gradient/image backgrounds, but the core is a measurable ratio, so humanJudgmentNeeded is false.
patterns.realWorldNote: Dawn audits specifically flag 'color contrast failures on sale badges and disabled elements' and multiple elements failing AA contrast. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-dawn-theme-accessibility

patterns.platform: Bootstrap default theme (buttons, alerts, form-validation, placeholders)
patterns.name: Default palette variants fail contrast (btn-warning, btn-info, alerts, placeholder)
patterns.description: Bootstrap's stock color variants — notably .btn-warning, .btn-info, .btn-success (dark text or white text on light fills) and muted placeholder text — produce text and UI-component contrast below 4.5:1 / 3:1 against light backgrounds. Sites that adopt the defaults unmodified inherit the failures across every page.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
<button class="btn btn-warning">Continue</button>
<!-- #ffc107 fill with near-black text region edges; white-text variants ~2-3:1 -->
<input class="form-control" placeholder="Search...">
<!-- placeholder ~ #6c757d on white -->
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: This one IS reliably automatable — axe/Lighthouse compute text contrast ratios and flag failing button/placeholder colors. Flagged false because a contrast checker catches it; the only caveat is large-text thresholds and overlay images, which can need human review.
patterns.realWorldNote: Bootstrap's own accessibility page admits default palette combinations may fall below WCAG contrast; twbs/bootstrap issue #25126 tracks failing AA combinations. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/25126

patterns.name: Placeholder used as the only label
patterns.description: Inputs styled by component libraries frequently use the placeholder attribute as the sole label (no <label>, no aria-label). The hint disappears once the user types, low-contrast placeholder text fails contrast, and there is no programmatic label — screen readers may announce nothing or only "edit text".
patterns.typicalMarkup:
<input type="email" placeholder="Email address">
<!-- no <label for>, no aria-label; placeholder is the only cue -->
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe reliably flags inputs with no accessible name ("Form elements must have labels"), so the bare missing-label case is automatable — flagged false. The residual judgment (is a placeholder an ADEQUATE instruction even when a label exists, contrast of the placeholder) can still need a human, but detection of no-label is a linter check.
patterns.realWorldNote: WCAG 3.3.2 and broad guidance treat placeholder-as-label as a failure (text vanishes on input, low contrast); extremely common in utility-CSS/component-styled forms.

patterns.platform: WebAIM Million corpus (all builders) — body text, theme palettes, image-overlay hero captions
patterns.name: Low-contrast text, including text over background images
patterns.description: Foreground/background color pairs fall below 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text). The hardest variant for tools is text laid over a photographic/gradient background or in CSS pseudo-elements, where there is no single solid background color to measure.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Subtle gray caption

Welcome
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Solid-color contrast IS reliably caught — it is the single most-detected error and the canonical automatable check (flagged humanJudgmentNeeded=false). BUT the text-over-image / gradient / overlapping-element variant is routinely MISSED because tools cannot determine the actual background pixels behind the text; that subset effectively needs human/visual judgment.
patterns.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million 2025: low contrast is the #1 error, on 79.1% of pages, 29.6 instances each: https://webaim.org/projects/million/2025 . Tools' inability to evaluate text over images is widely documented: https://www.davidmello.com/software-testing/test-automation/playwright-accessibility-testing-axe-lighthouse-limitations

patterns.platform: Form fields in CMS form builders and templates (WordPress/Webflow forms, custom inputs) where the placeholder is the only label
patterns.name: placeholder used as the only label / instruction
patterns.description: An input has no <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby — only a placeholder. The placeholder is low-contrast, vanishes on focus/typing (so users lose the field's name mid-entry), is not consistently treated as an accessible name by all AT, and offers no persistent instruction. Often paired with required-field and format hints living only in the placeholder.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Browsers may expose placeholder as a fallback accessible name, so some scanners report a name present and pass it (axe does warn in some configs, but inconsistently across the suite). The disappearing-on-input UX failure and the lost-instruction problem are behavioral/visual and need human judgment; the contrast of placeholder text is also an easily-missed visual check.
patterns.realWorldNote: MDN/WebAIM and reform.app 'Common ARIA Mistakes in Forms' document placeholder-as-label as a top form anti-pattern. https://www.reform.app/blog/common-aria-mistakes-in-forms-and-fixes
